questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which combination of CSS properties creates a NEW Stacking Context for descendant z-index positioning?

options.A: opacity less than 1, transform not none, or filter not none

questions.explanation: Non-1 opacity, 2D/3D transforms, filters, containment, or isolation properties create new stacking contexts.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: If element A has `z-index: 9999;` inside stacking context X (which has `z-index: 1;`), and element B has `z-index: 2;` inside root context, which renders on top?

options.A: Element B, because parent context X (z-index 1) is lower than B's parent context (z-index 2)

questions.explanation: Child z-indexes are local to their parent stacking context; parent context comparison overrides child values.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the specificity weight of the `:is(h1, .title, #header)` pseudo-class selector?

options.A: Takes specificity of its most specific argument (`#header` -> 1, 0, 0)

questions.explanation: The `:is()` pseudo-class takes the specificity of its single most specific argument inside the parameter list.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the specificity weight of the `:where(h1, .title, #header)` pseudo-class selector?

options.A: Always exactly (0, 0, 0)

questions.explanation: Unlike `:is()`, `:where()` replaced specificity is always strictly zero (0, 0, 0).

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));` do?

options.A: Creates responsive grid columns that collapse empty tracks and stretch filled columns to fit container

questions.explanation: auto-fit drops empty tracks and stretches filled tracks; minmax guarantees column responsiveness without media queries.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the difference between `auto-fill` and `auto-fit` in CSS Grid `minmax()` track repeaters?

options.A: `auto-fill` keeps empty track gaps in layout; `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks to 0px allowing filled tracks to expand

questions.explanation: auto-fill retains empty tracks taking space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks so remaining items stretch across container.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: In Flexbox, what does `flex-shrink: 0;` prevent a flex item from doing when container overflows?

options.A: Prevents the flex item from shrinking below its flex-basis size
options.B: Prevents the flex item from growing

questions.explanation: flex-shrink: 0 disables item compression, enforcing item initial basis dimensions.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How is extra remaining free space distributed among flex items with `flex-grow: 1` and `flex-grow: 2`?

options.A: Item with flex-grow: 2 gets twice as much OF THE REMAINING FREE SPACE as item with flex-grow: 1
options.B: Item 2 is twice as wide total as Item 1

questions.explanation: flex-grow ratio dictates proportion distribution of remaining free container space, not total absolute width.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Can CSS custom properties (variables) be inherited down the DOM tree?

options.A: Yes, custom properties inherit by default like font-family or color
options.B: No, variables are scoped strictly to declaring selector

questions.explanation: CSS custom properties are standard cascading inherited properties.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the fallback mechanism syntax for `var()` if a custom property is undefined?

options.A: var(--main-color, #333)

questions.explanation: The second parameter in var(--name, fallback) serves as fallback value if custom property is invalid/undefined.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Inheritance and the CSS box model
questions.question: Which CSS property controls container query styling based on ancestor box size instead of viewport size?

options.A: container-type: inline-size;

questions.explanation: container-type: inline-size (or normal/size) establishes a container context for `@container` media queries.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Functions such as calc(), min(), max(), and clamp()
questions.question: What happens if mathematical expression inside `calc()` lacks spaces around `+` or `-` operators (e.g. `calc(100%-10px)`)?

options.A: Expression is invalid and property declaration is ignored

questions.explanation: CSS calc() strictly requires whitespace around `+` and `-` operators to differentiate from signed unit tokens.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which modern pseudo-class matches parent elements that contain specific descendant elements?

options.A: :has()

questions.explanation: The `:has()` relational pseudo-class tests if parent contains descendants matching selector parameter.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `p:not(.featured)` select?

options.A: All paragraph elements that do NOT have the class 'featured'

questions.explanation: The `:not()` negation pseudo-class selects elements that fail to match parameter selector.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property prevents unwanted flickers and enforces hardware GPU acceleration layer creation during 3D transforms?

options.A: will-change: transform;

questions.explanation: will-change hints browser ahead of time to allocate dedicated GPU compositor layers.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `backface-visibility: hidden;` do during 3D card flipping transforms?

options.A: Hides reverse mirror side of element box when rotated away from viewer facing

questions.explanation: backface-visibility: hidden prevents displaying reverse side mirror image when element is rotated in 3D space.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What happens when `animation-direction: alternate;` is applied to an repeating keyframe animation?

options.A: Animation cycles forward on odd iterations and reverses backward on even iterations

questions.explanation: alternate reverses playback direction every subsequent cycle iteration.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property enforces smooth snap points when scrolling through horizontal card carousels?

options.A: scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;

questions.explanation: scroll-snap-type (on container) and scroll-snap-align (on children) enforce touch carousel scroll snapping.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property visually hides content on screen while keeping it accessible to screen reader voice synthesisers?

options.A: Clip-path / sr-only CSS pattern (position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0);)

questions.explanation: The sr-only/visually-hidden utility pattern clips rendering bounds without removing node from accessibility tree.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the CSS `subgrid` feature in CSS Grid layout level 2?

options.A: Allows nested grid items to inherit track definition lines and alignment directly from parent grid

questions.explanation: grid-template-columns: subgrid allows nested child grids to participate in parent track alignment.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `:focus-within` match?

options.A: An element if the element itself or ANY of its descendants currently has focus

questions.explanation: :focus-within matches container elements whenever any nested child element receives focus.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `:focus-visible` match compared to standard `:focus`?

options.A: Matches focus indicator state ONLY when browser heuristics determine focus should be visibly indicated (e.g., keyboard tab navigation)

questions.explanation: :focus-visible avoids drawing focus rings on mouse clicks while displaying them for keyboard tab users.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS declaration forces an element onto its own hardware-accelerated GPU Compositor layer?

options.A: transform: translateZ(0);

questions.explanation: translateZ(0) or translate3d(0,0,0) triggers GPU layer promotion in browser rendering engine.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How do you prevent flex items from shrinking smaller than their inner content size?

options.A: Set `min-width: 0;` or `flex-shrink: 0;` depending on desired container behavior

questions.explanation: Flex items have `min-width: auto` default; setting min-width: 0 allows flex shrinking below content size when clipping.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Units: px, em, rem, %, vw, and vh
questions.question: What is the difference between `ch` and `ex` units in CSS?

options.A: `ch` is width of character '0'; `ex` is x-height of current font font-size
options.B: `ch` is column height; `ex` is exact pixels

questions.explanation: ch equals width of character '0', ex equals x-height of lowercase 'x' in active font.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the result of `margin-top` applied on an inline element like `<span>` without altering display property?

options.A: Top and bottom margins have NO effect on inline non-replaced elements
options.B: Pushes content down by margin height

questions.explanation: Vertical margins (top/bottom) have no layout effect on non-replaced inline elements.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `isolation: isolate;` do in CSS?

options.A: Creates a new stacking context explicitly without requiring transforms or opacity changes

questions.explanation: isolation: isolate creates a new stacking context safely without visual side effects.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `align-content` do in Flexbox?

options.A: Aligns multi-line flex tracks along cross axis when extra space exists
options.B: Aligns single items inside flex row

questions.explanation: align-content controls spacing between multiple line tracks in wrapped flex containers.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the effect of `grid-auto-flow: dense;` in a grid layout?

options.A: Attempts to fill in visual grid gaps earlier in layout if smaller items fit later

questions.explanation: dense packing algorithm backfills empty grid gaps with smaller out-of-order items.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property controls how background image colors mix with element background colors?

options.A: background-blend-mode

questions.explanation: background-blend-mode blends background images and colors of a single element box.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property controls how an element's content blends with layers behind it across DOM elements?

options.A: mix-blend-mode

questions.explanation: mix-blend-mode defines blending between an element and its underlying parent DOM elements.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is cubic-bezier timing function `transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1);`?

options.A: Mathematical Bézier curve defining transition velocity speed rate acceleration profile over time

questions.explanation: cubic-bezier defines custom acceleration easing curves for transitions/animations.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What is the aspect-ratio property introduced in modern CSS?

options.A: Explicitly sets preferred width-to-height ratio for box sizing (`aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;`)

questions.explanation: aspect-ratio sets a target dimensional aspect ratio for box sizing calculations.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `@property` at-rule in modern CSS allow developers to do?

options.A: Explicitly define custom property types, initial values, and inheritance behavior for CSS variable animation

questions.explanation: @property registers CSS custom properties with strict type syntax checking and animatable data types.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Inheritance and the CSS box model
questions.question: What does `all: unset;` do on an element?

options.A: Resets all CSS properties to inherited values if inherited, or initial values if non-inherited

questions.explanation: all: unset resets all element CSS declarations to inherit/initial default behavior.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Inheritance and the CSS box model
questions.question: What does `all: revert;` do?

options.A: Rolls back all property values to default browser user-agent stylesheet origin values

questions.explanation: revert rolls back properties to user-agent default browser styles.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What causes Layout Thrashing in JavaScript DOM interactions?

options.A: Interleaving repetitive DOM writes followed immediately by synchronous DOM layout reads forcing recalculations

questions.explanation: Repeated write-then-read cycles force browsers to perform forced synchronous layout recalculations.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: How do you prevent text wrapping on line breaks inside a flex or block container?

options.A: white-space: nowrap;

questions.explanation: white-space: nowrap prevents text content from wrapping onto new lines.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `::marker` pseudo-element style?

options.A: The bullet point or number indicator box of list items (`<li>`)

questions.explanation: ::marker targets bullet points or numbers of list items.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `::selection` style?

options.A: The visual portion of document highlighted/selected by user pointer cursor

questions.explanation: ::selection customizes background and color of text selected by user pointer.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which value of `animation-play-state` pauses an ongoing CSS keyframe animation?

options.A: animation-play-state: paused;

questions.explanation: animation-play-state: paused halts animation keyframe execution at current timestamp.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property specifies alignment of ENTIRE grid columns tracks within container along inline axis?

options.A: justify-content

questions.explanation: justify-content aligns entire grid track layout within grid container horizontally.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which property specifies alignment of content INSIDE individual grid cells horizontally?

options.A: justify-items

questions.explanation: justify-items aligns item elements inside their assigned grid area cells along inline axis.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `overscroll-behavior: contain;` prevent?

options.A: Prevents scroll chaining overflow from passing to parent body scroll container when edge is reached

questions.explanation: overscroll-behavior: contain prevents scroll boundary propagation (scroll chaining) to parent scrollports.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which CSS property controls optical kerning and ligatures in advanced font rendering?

options.A: font-feature-settings

questions.explanation: font-feature-settings and font-kerning configure OpenType font ligatures and kerning features.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: Which value of `font-display` minimizes Flash of Unstyled Text (FOUT) by rendering invisible text briefly during web font load?

options.A: font-display: swap;

questions.explanation: font-display: swap uses fallback system font immediately, swapping custom font when loaded.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What happens when two CSS selectors have IDENTICAL specificity weight and apply to same element?

options.A: The selector declared LATER in CSS document order wins and applies styles

questions.explanation: When specificity is tied, the rule appearing last in document source order takes precedence.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Functions such as calc(), min(), max(), and clamp()
questions.question: What does `min(50vw, 500px)` return for element width?

options.A: Returns whichever value is SMALLER between 50vw and 500px

questions.explanation: min() selects the minimum calculated value among parameters.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.topic: Functions such as calc(), min(), max(), and clamp()
questions.question: What does `max(10vw, 300px)` return for element width?

options.A: Returns whichever value is LARGER between 10vw and 300px

questions.explanation: max() selects the maximum calculated value among parameters.

questions.subject: CSS
questions.question: What does `writing-mode: vertical-rl;` do to text flow layout?

options.A: Changes inline text flow orientation to vertical running top-to-bottom, right-to-left

questions.explanation: writing-mode configures text line orientation (e.g. vertical-rl for East Asian layout).
